newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * The government's control body has issued a series of reports accusing former government and local officials of using their offices in order to get land properties, mainly in lakeside residential areas around Bucharest.
The report singles out former agriculture and interior ministry officials, bankers, Bucharest city hall officials, alleged to have purchased land illegally to build posh villas.
The report says some 11,000 hectares of valuable land were illegally acquired by dignitaries.
* Valerian Stan, head of the government's control body, said the report was meant to expose illegal deals in the public administration sector and to protect private property.

* Interior Minister Gavril Dejeu criticised local court rulings to have people arrested for serious crimes released from police custody on medical grounds, saying these rulings jeopardise police efforts to track down major corruption cases.

* Bucharest's municipal court ruled on Friday to release former Bancorex bank chief Razvan Temesan who was arrested last month pending investigations on suspicions of misdeeds which allegedly caused 1.4 billion lei in losses to the bank.
Temesan will stay in custody pending a court ruling on prosecutors' appeal against his release, the radio said.
